DEDR 3263: Kannada tiṇḍi, Tamil tiṇṭi and Tulu tīnů/tīni belong to the Dravidian eat/food word-family; the listed Proto-Dravidian form is the verbal root. DEDR 3263 records Proto-Dravidian *tiHn- ‘to eat’; Tamil tiṇṭi ‘eatables’, Kannada tiṇḍi ‘food’ and Tulu tīnů/tīni ‘food, meal’. The cognate family is clear, though the nominal meanings are not identical in every language.

DEDR 1911 identifies Kannada kūḻ (ಕೂಳು) ‘boiled rice, food’ as part of Proto-Dravidian *kūḻ ‘porridge’. Tamil kūḻ means thick gruel/porridge; Tulu kūru/kūlu/kūḷu means boiled rice. This is a genuine cognate set, but the meanings range from porridge to boiled rice and food; it should not be treated as an exact synonym for every use of ‘food’.
